$comment: Public-organization cutover controller state (SECB-WP-FWK-080, issue #143). THIS FILE PERFORMS NO EXTERNAL EFFECT. It does not transfer a repository, change visibility, create a ruleset, enable a merge queue, or attest an artifact. It records where the cutover stands and refuses transitions that are not evidenced. Every capability is tracked separately: one capability becoming available NEVER raises the state of another, because they are configured through different surfaces and fail independently.

what_this_is_not.not_an_approval: Recording DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZED requires an Agentic Decision Receipt this file cannot mint. Authority comes from an effective delegated mandate exercised by independent agents, not from a human approving each instance -- and not from an executor writing its own authorization.
what_this_is_not.not_a_capability_probe: live_readback is NOT_OBSERVED throughout. No external call is permitted at this state, so every capability's real status is unmeasured -- declared, not assumed absent.
what_this_is_not.not_enforcement: Nothing consumes this manifest at merge time. Its only consumer is a validator and a test.

irreversibility.visibility_change: Making the repository public exposes Actions run history and job logs. Secrecy is not restorable by reverting visibility: anything disclosed may have been fetched, cached or indexed.
irreversibility.consequence: DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZED is the one transition that cannot be undone by a later transition, which is why it is gated on a verifiable receipt rather than on capability readiness. Irreversibility raises the evidence bar; it does not hand the decision to a different actor.
irreversibility.prerequisite: Credential cutover (issue #115, WP-05) must complete first. A secret that is still live when logs become public is disclosed, not rotated.

rulesets.purpose: Branch protection equivalent -- required checks, merge restrictions
rulesets.measured: branches/main/protection returns 403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public

live_readback.reason: no external call permitted at DISCLOSURE_UNAPPROVED

merge_queue.purpose: Serialize merges and test the combined queue head

live_readback.reason: no external call permitted at DISCLOSURE_UNAPPROVED

merge_queue.blocking_prerequisite: ci.yml declares no merge_group trigger, and three of four jobs are gated on github.event_name == 'pull_request', so they would be SKIPPED on a merge-group event. Enabling the queue before that is fixed produces skipped required checks. See issue #118.
merge_queue.membership_proof: NOT_PROVEN -- no documented field binds an ordered PR list to the event group-head SHA. Ref-name parsing and commit topology are prohibited as substitutes.

artifact_attestations.measured: available for public repositories on Free/Pro/Team; this repository is private

live_readback.reason: no external call permitted at DISCLOSURE_UNAPPROVED

artifact_attestations.blocking_prerequisite: Producing an attestation grants nothing until a consumer verifies signature, timestamp and signer identity. Generation is not provenance.

archival.purpose: Immutable retention of evidence outside the working repository

live_readback.reason: no external call permitted at DISCLOSURE_UNAPPROVED

evidence_lifecycle.why_not_restated: Copying the stage list would create a second definition that drifts from the first. This manifest cites the source and adds nothing to it; the stage vocabulary is that file's to define. The claim-strength axis it plugs into is issue #124, also unmerged.

independent_obligations.subject: L0-GIT-004 -- prohibit non-fast-forward update of a canonical ref
TR-01 Transition Evidence Receipt, and the merge_group activation note

agentic_authorization.model: EFFECTIVE_DELEGATED_MANDATE + INDEPENDENT_AGENTIC_DECISION + SNAPSHOT_BOUND_RECEIPT + LEAST_PRIVILEGE_EFFECT_EXECUTOR + INDEPENDENT_POST_EFFECT_READBACK = AGENTICALLY_AUTHORIZED_EFFECT

separation_rules.executor_is_not_a_ballot_agent: An agent that decided may not perform the effect. Otherwise the decision and its execution share a failure mode and one compromised actor carries both.
separation_rules.readback_verifier_is_not_the_executor: The actor that made the change may not certify that the change is what was decided -- the producer/consumer boundary applied to an external effect.

snapshot_binding.stale_rule: If any bound field differs from the observed snapshot at execution time, the receipt is STALE and the effect is refused. A decision is about a state, not about a repository in general.
snapshot_binding.mandate_source_state: ABSENT FROM main -- authored on the #113 DAAF-intake branch and unmerged. Until it lands there is no mandate digest to bind, so no receipt can be complete. Declared rather than stubbed: a placeholder digest would make an unsatisfiable precondition look satisfied.

post_effect.why: An API returning 200 proves a call was accepted, not that the resulting state is the one decided. Readback is a separate observation by a separate actor.

identity_separation.reason: Seven distinct actor_id STRINGS in a receipt prove nothing: a single account can write any string into a JSON file, exactly as one session can type any role banner. That is the self-approval-in-five-hats defect the ballot layer already refuses. What would prove separation is a structural platform actor field -- distinct GitHub App identities, which rulesets can name as actors -- not text inside the artifact being authorized.
identity_separation.consequence: The validator refuses DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZED while this is UNPROVEN. This is NOT a reversion to per-instance human approval: the authority model is agentic, and what is missing is the identity substrate the model requires.
not_proven: that Administration(write) confers decision authority -- it is a capability
that OIDC id-token:write permits resource modification -- it is an identity
that generating an attestation verifies one -- signature, timestamp and signer identity must each be checked by a consumer
